les: Warm, roer en fyn: vinniger oplos
kaps_punt: Die tempo van oplossing: faktore wat die tempo (tyd wat dit neem) van oplossing beïnvloed: temperatuur van die mengsel; die mengsel te roer of te skud; korrelgrootte van die opgeloste stof

items.bewering: Hoe vinnig 'n stof oplos, noem ons die tempo van oplossing. Ons meet dit aan die tyd totdat geen korrels meer oor is nie. ... Hoe korter die tyd, hoe vinniger los die stof op.
items.bron: Lumen Learning CHEM101 'Rate of Dissolving' (courses.lumenlearning.com/umes-cheminter/chapter/rate-of-dissolving/) - rate of dissolving as how quickly a given quantity dissolves; a shorter time to dissolve the same amount is a faster rate, so time and rate are inversely related. The lesson's own CAPS bullet also defines tempo as 'tyd wat dit neem'.

items.bewering: 'n Korrel sout bestaan uit baie deeltjies wat styf teen mekaar gepak is. Die water se deeltjies is naby mekaar en beweeg heeltyd verby mekaar.
items.bron: Purdue University General Chemistry Help, 'States of Matter' and 'Gases, Liquids, and Solids' (chem.purdue.edu/gchelp) - solid particles tightly packed in a regular pattern; liquid particles close together but able to slide past each other.

items.bewering: Hulle kom aanhoudend teen die buitekant van die korrel aan. Daar raak die sout se deeltjies een vir een los en versprei tussen die water se deeltjies. Die deeltjies binne-in die korrel kan eers losraak wanneer die buitenste lae weg is. Oplos gebeur dus net waar die korrel aan die water raak. Die korrel word van buite na binne kleiner.
items.bron: Lumen Learning 'Rate of Dissolving': 'Dissolving is a surface phenomenon since it depends on solvent molecules colliding with the outer surface of the solute.' PMC11483817 'Crumbling crystals: on the dissolution mechanism of NaCl in water' - steady ion-by-ion loss from the crystal surface; ions pulled free are surrounded by water (hydration). The late 'crumbling' in that paper concerns nanoscale crystals and does not bear on a visible grain.

items.bewering: Suiker en sout los vinniger op in warm water as in koue water.
items.bron: Lumen Learning 'Rate of Dissolving' (heating the solvent increases the rate of dissolving); The Naked Scientists, 'Why do salts dissolve better in warm water, but not gases?' (thenakedscientists.com). Note the claim is about RATE, which is correct for salt even though NaCl's solubility changes little with temperature (about 36 g/100 mL at 0 C to 39 g/100 mL at 100 C, ausetute.com.au solubility table); the lesson does not claim more salt dissolves.

items.bewering: In warmer water beweeg die deeltjies vinniger rond. Die water se deeltjies kom dus meer dikwels teen die korrel aan. So raak die korrel se deeltjies gouer los.
items.bron: Lumen Learning 'Rate of Dissolving': 'Heating up the solvent gives the molecules more kinetic energy. The more rapid motion means that the solvent molecules collide with the solute with greater frequency and the collisions occur with more force.' The lesson states the frequency half only; that is a simplification, not an error.

items.bewering: Die losgemaakte deeltjies beweeg ook vinniger van die korrel af weg. Dan kan die volgende laag van die korrel gouer aan die beurt kom.
items.bron: EBSCO Research Starters 'Diffusion in Gases and Liquids' - molecular diffusion is faster at higher temperature; together with the surface-phenomenon source (Lumen) this supports detached particles clearing the surface faster and exposing the next layer sooner.

items.bewering: As jy die water roer, los die suiker vinniger op. Jy kan ook sout en water in 'n toe bottel skud.
items.bron: Lumen Learning 'Rate of Dissolving': 'Dissolving sugar in water will occur more quickly if the water is stirred.' CK-12 'Rate of Dissolving' (flexbooks.ck12.org) lists stirring/agitation among the factors; shaking a closed container is agitation of the same kind.

items.bewering: Die water reg om die korrel raak vol deeltjies wat reeds opgelos het. Sulke water neem nuwe deeltjies stadiger op. Wanneer jy roer, dra die bewegende water daardie vol water weg. Water met min opgeloste deeltjies kom dan tot teen die korrel.
items.bron: CK-12 Flexi 'Why does stirring increase the rate of dissolution?' and Membrane Solutions 'Stirring and Dissolving Rate' - unstirred, the water at the solute surface becomes (near-)saturated and further dissolving slows; stirring thins that layer and brings fresh solvent to the surface. Lumen: 'stirring allows fresh solvent molecules to continually be in contact with the solute.' The mapping (concentrated layer carried away, fresh water arrives) matches the accepted diffusion-layer account.

items.bewering: Roer maak nie die deeltjies vinniger soos warmte doen nie. Sonder roer los die suiker steeds op, net stadiger.
items.bron: Lumen Learning 'Rate of Dissolving' attributes the temperature effect to increased molecular kinetic energy and the stirring effect to renewing solvent contact, not to raising particle speed; stirring by hand does not measurably heat the water. Dissolution without stirring proceeds by diffusion, only more slowly (CK-12 Flexi on stirring; unstirred hot/cold salt trials in search results dissolved fully).

items.bewering: Dieselfde hoeveelheid fyn sout los vinniger op as growwe sout.
items.bron: Lumen Learning 'Rate of Dissolving': 'A given quantity of solute dissolves faster when it is ground into small particles than if it is in the form of a large chunk because more surface area is exposed.'

items.bewering: 'n Growwe korrel het baie deeltjies binne-in wat nog nie by die water kan uitkom nie. Verdeel jy dieselfde sout in baie klein korreltjies, raak baie meer daarvan op een slag aan die water. Meer deeltjies kan dus tegelyk losraak.
items.bron: Lumen Learning 'Rate of Dissolving' (surface area exposed; dissolving is a surface phenomenon); CK-12 'Rate of Dissolving' (smaller particles expose more surface area to the solvent).

items.bewering: Die sout se deeltjies self is in albei presies dieselfde. Net die korrels verskil in grootte.
items.bron: Follows from the block's own premise ('Verdeel jy dieselfde sout'): grinding changes grain size, not the substance; the particles (Na+ and Cl- ions) are identical (PMC11483817 on NaCl's ionic lattice). The sentence refers to the same salt divided, so additives in commercial fine salt do not make it false.

items.bewering: Jy neem twee glase met elk 'n halwe koppie (125 ml) water. In albei gooi jy een teelepel (5 ml) van dieselfde sout.
items.bron: Lancewood conversion table (lancewood.co.za/conversion-table) and Radio Islam measurements chart (radioislam.org.za) - South African metric cup 250 ml, teaspoon 5 ml; half a cup is 125 ml. A 5 ml teaspoon of salt (about 6 g) is far below NaCl's solubility in 125 ml even when cold (about 36 g/100 mL at 0 C, ausetute.com.au), so both glasses can dissolve it fully and the test is workable.

items.bewering: Nou verskil net die temperatuur en al die ander dinge bly dieselfde. As jy ook die warm glas geroer het, het twee dinge tegelyk verskil. Dan weet jy nie watter een die tyd korter gemaak het nie. 'n Toets wat net een ding op 'n slag verander, is 'n regverdige toets.
items.bron: Science Buddies 'Doing a Fair Test: Variables for Beginners' (sciencebuddies.org) and Let's Talk Science 'Setting Up a Fair Test' (letstalkscience.ca) - a fair test changes one variable and keeps all others the same so the result can be attributed to that variable; changing two at once confounds the result.

items.bewering: tempo van oplossing: Hoe vinnig 'n stof oplos. Jy meet dit aan die tyd wat dit neem om heeltemal op te los.
items.bron: Lumen Learning 'Rate of Dissolving' (rate = how quickly a given quantity dissolves); time to dissolve completely is a standard measure of it. Read alone, the entry fits nothing else.

items.bewering: korrelgrootte: Hoe groot die korrels van 'n vaste stof is, soos growwe of fyn sout.
items.bron: Lumen Learning / CK-12 'Rate of Dissolving' (particle size of the solute, e.g. granulated vs powdered); plain meaning of grain size.

items.bewering: regverdige toets: 'n Toets waarin jy net een ding verander en al die ander dinge dieselfde hou.
items.bron: Science Buddies 'Doing a Fair Test: Variables for Beginners'; Let's Talk Science 'Setting Up a Fair Test'.

items.bewering: deeltjie: Een van die piepklein stukkies waaruit alle materie bestaan. Dit is te klein om selfs met 'n vergrootglas te sien.
items.bron: Purdue 'States of Matter' (all matter made of particles); Javalab 'Why we can't see atoms under an optical microscope' (javalab.org) - atoms are about 0.1-0.3 nm, far below the ~500 nm limit of light optics, so neither a magnifying glass nor a light microscope can show them. The claim is true a fortiori ('selfs met 'n vergrootglas').

items.bewering: oplos: Wanneer die deeltjies van 'n stof losraak en tussen die deeltjies van 'n vloeistof meng, sodat jy geen korrels meer kan sien nie.
items.bron: PMC11483817 (ions leave the crystal and are dispersed among and surrounded by water molecules); Lumen 'Rate of Dissolving'. Read alone it does not describe melting (no second liquid) or a suspension (particles do not separate to particle level). Adequate for Grade 6.

items.bewering: Superlatiewe en analogieë: die les bevat geen superlatief (eerste, oudste, grootste, vinnigste, enigste) nie en geen eli10-blok of vergelyking nie; die enigste universele bewering ('alle materie') is hierbo by 'deeltjie' nagegaan.
items.bron: Every block read end to end for superlatives and comparisons; none found. 'alle materie' checked against Purdue 'States of Matter'.

opsomming: Every claim in the lesson checked out against sources, including the particle explanations of why heat, stirring and fine grains speed dissolving, the 125 ml and 5 ml measures, and the fair-test definition; there are no superlatives or analogies, and nothing needs fixing.
